content:
Maria Gomez: P1 escalation from ACME Analytics — their SSE streams are disconnecting mid-response and then they get 429 on resume. They say partial output + double token charge. Ticket attached.

Maria Gomez: Symptoms from customer:
- Stream emits chunks for ~10-18s then connection closes with HTTP 200 (no 5xx)
- The last SSE event before close is a partial delta (truncated sentence)
- Client reconnects with `Last-Event-ID: evt-67890` and immediate response body is 429 JSON (not a retryable SSE event)
- Billing shows they were charged for original stream and for the resumed stream; total tokens > tokens in final assembled text

Maria Gomez: Repro steps they gave (hosted):
1) Start SSE via curl
```
curl -N -v -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-acme-rotating-xxxx" \
  -H "Accept: text/event-stream" \
  -H "Last-Event-ID: evt-0" \
  "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/stream?model=gpt-open-1"
```
2) After ~12s connection drops. Client reads last event id `evt-67890` and reconnects with that id.
3) Resume request returns 429 body like:
```
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
Content-Type: application/json
X-Request-Id: 01J9AAAABCDE

{ "error": "rate_limit_exceeded", "code": "RATE_LIMIT_EXCEEDED", "retry_after": 15 }
```
Customer proxy logs show:
- orig req id: req=01J9AAAABCDA  ; resume req id: req=01J9AAAABCE
- upstream nginx logged `upstream prematurely closed connection while reading upstream` for the original
- client sees `event: message\ndata: {"delta":"..."}\n\n` then socket reset

Jake Patel: pinging eng-runtime and eng-infra — can you triage? cc @eng-oncall

Anika Cho: Billing POC here. We already saw ACME charge spike. I'll suspend further auto-billing for that account until we confirm root cause. Please add any request ids so we can tie tokens.

Jake Patel: Notes from quick glance:
- Could be we're counting tokens on request acceptance (token estimate) and again when resume is accepted. Need to check where token accounting increments happen: at request start vs on finalization.
- Also suspicious that resume returned 429 immediately. Why would rate limiter kick in for a resume from same session? Maybe the resume path is routed to a different rate-limit bucket or we don't decrement in-flight reservations on disconnect.

infra-bot: streaming-service cluster `streams-prod-4` reported transient connection resets at 2026-03-14T03:12:18Z. Upstreams show TCP RSTs to container 10.12.45.9:8080.

Nate (eng-infra): I pulled rate-limiter metrics for ACME org (org_id=acme-123): burst quota exhausted at 03:12:19, then LOTS of resume attempts within 20s window. Rate limiter policy is token-bucket with reservation on accept; looks like we reserve on accept and do not release on socket close -> potential double charge when resumed.

Jake Patel: That matches billing symptom. Repro idea: run two streams in parallel that are same session and force disconnect then resume twice; check billing ledger entries for same session.

Maria Gomez: Customer attached SSE payload snippet — last chunk before drop:
```
event: message
id: evt-67890
data: {"delta":" ...middle of sentence here, predicting token 2345\n"}

// socket close
```

Anika Cho: Can we generate a provisional credit for acme-analytics for the duplicated tokens? They flagged this as P1. I'll put a hold on the invoice and create a credit case, but will await eng confirmation of root cause before issuing full refund.

Jake Patel: Immediate mitigations we should try:
- Disable reservation-on-accept for streaming endpoints (fall back to charge-on-completion) OR
- On disconnect, release reserved tokens immediately in rate-limiter store for that session id
- Allow a short resume window where we honor Last-Event-ID and do not count it as new acceptance requiring reservation

Ops-oncall (Rosa): I can patch a config in rate-limiter to release on disconnect for a single experiment cluster. Which flag? `release_on_disconnect=true`? Any safety concerns? We might undercount if clients legitimately reconnect and we had already accounted for tokens used.

Jake Patel: Safety: make the change behind a feature flag and target a small percentage of traffic or dev cluster. We need metrics on double-charge occurrences.

infra-bugbot: Created issue INFRA-2029 "reserve-on-accept -> potential double-charge on SSE resume" and linked logs (req=01J9AAAABCDA, 01J9AAAABCE).

Rosa (ops-oncall): Rolling config to canary (streams-canary) with `release_on_disconnect=true` now. Will watch rate-limiter meter `reserved_tokens` and `released_on_disconnect`.

Jake Patel: Eng-runtime action items:
- Add diagnostic logging on stream lifecycle: when we reserve tokens, include session_id and request_id and emit `reserved:<n>` and `release_on_disconnect` events
- Reproduce locally with client that writes Last-Event-ID resume
- Validate that resumed request does not double-reserve tokens

Anika Cho: Billing action items:
- Freeze charges for acme-analytics account
- Await eng confirmation; if duplicate reservations are found, we will issue a credit and backfill

Maria Gomez: Customer-facing proposal (will wait for eng confirm): "We're investigating a rate-limiter edge-case where our reservation logic may double-count tokens on resumed streams. We've paused billing for your account and will issue a credit if duplicate charges are confirmed. Our eng team is rolling a canary fix and will follow up in the next 2 hours." :white_check_mark:

Jake Patel: Repro plan (eng-runtime):
1) Start SSE with curl or node client, record Last-Event-ID
2) Force SIGKILL of server connection to simulate abrupt close
3) Reconnect with `Last-Event-ID` and confirm server path: is it `resume` route or regular `stream`? Ensure both hit same rate-limiter codepath
4) Check ledger writes: ledger.write happens on reserve and on finalize. Add debug flag to skip ledger.write on resume accept during test.

Rosa: Can the oncall team provide an example of the resume request headers we should look for in the ingress logs? I saw Last-Event-ID but any other hints?

Maria Gomez: Customer says they set `Last-Event-ID` to the SSE id value and keep `session-id: s-ACME-1001` header on reconnects.

Jake Patel: Good. We'll grep ingress nginx logs for `session-id` and those request ids. Also check our billing ledger for duplicate writes with same session-id + event id.

infra-bot: streams-canary metrics after 5m: `reserved_tokens` decreased by 92 on disconnect-release, `resume_429_count` from 7 -> 1 (expected). Will continue monitoring.

Jake Patel: Preliminary conclusion: rate-limiter was reserving tokens on accept and not releasing on sudden socket close; resume path did a fresh reservation and that produced double-charging behavior. Canary appears to reduce resume 429s by releasing reserved tokens on disconnect. Need eng-runtime code change to ensure release-on-disconnect is robust and idempotent.

Anika Cho: I'll prepare provisional credit for ACME (estimate 1,200 tokens) and will finalize after eng confirms exact duplicated amount.

Maria Gomez: Thanks team. I'll update ACME ticket with this interim status and ETA 2 hours for follow-up. If anyone finds contradictory data ping me directly. :phone: 

Participants: Maria Gomez, Jake Patel, Anika Cho, Rosa (ops-oncall), infra-bot, infra-bugbot, ops-oncall, eng-oncall, support-bot
